title: How Millionaires Spend a Normal Tuesday
description:
Most American millionaires didn't inherit a cent, and their Tuesday looks a lot like yours: the alarm, the commute, the job, dinner at home. In this video we walk through a normal millionaire's Tuesday hour by hour and find 20 small moments that build wealth, from three angles: the money numbers of the morning, the psychology of the workday, and the evening playbook you can copy tomorrow.

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

0:00 Intro
1:50 How we got the numbers
2:26 Angle 1: The Numbers (morning)
2:36 1. The money moved before they woke up
4:02 2. Coffee at home, mostly
5:10 3. A paid off car in the driveway
6:32 4. The commute is a classroom
7:38 5. Lunch from home, most days
8:31 6. They know their numbers
9:23 7. No impulse buys at work

10:54 8. They think like owners
11:49 9. Income is their biggest tool
12:45 10. They say no to most pitches
13:57 11. They don't keep up with coworkers
14:49 12. They think in decades
15:49 13. They protect their health
17:00 Angle 3: The Playbook (evening)
17:17 14. Dinner at home with family
18:07 15. Screens off, books on
19:02 16. A side project
19:50 17. Money talk with their partner
20:41 18. Tomorrow planned tonight
21:27 19. Gratitude, not envy
22:10 20. Sleep
22:59 What one Tuesday adds up to
23:58 Real quiet millionaires
25:32 The other Tuesday
26:31 Bonus: the once a month moments
28:01 Mistakes when copying the routine
28:58 Questions people ask
31:01 Recap: the 20 moments
31:40 What to do next

Sources:
- Ramsey Solutions, National Study of Millionaires (79% received no inheritance; most common careers; about 8 in 10 invested in their company retirement plan; average age reaching $1M about 49)
- Thomas J. Stanley and William D. Danko, The Millionaire Next Door (1996); Thomas J. Stanley, Stop Acting Rich (2009): median vehicle price about $31,000
- US Bureau of Labor Statistics, American Time Use Survey (TV is the top leisure activity, close to 3 hours a day)
- Edmunds, average new-vehicle monthly payment (above $700)
- Tom Corley, Rich Habits survey (small, self-reported sample)
- Federal Trade Commission, Consumer Sentinel fraud reports (investment scams among the costliest)
- Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, about 1 in 3 US adults don't get enough sleep
- Growth examples: monthly compounding at 7% average yearly return (illustration, not a promise)
